purpose: Verify that reference analysis transfers observable visual DNA while separating observation from uncertain hardware inference, preserving reference roles, and allowing target locks to override reference tendencies.

scoring.pass_condition: The result must state or encode what was observed, what is transferable, what remains reference-specific, what is uncertain, and which target locks override the reference. Exact hardware may be factual only when supported by user-supplied metadata or another authoritative source.
critical_failures: claiming an exact camera, lens, aperture, stock or LUT solely from image appearance
copying incidental subject matter or production details that were not assigned as transferable reference DNA
letting a style/light reference overwrite identity or product-geometry locks
averaging multiple references without explicit roles or priorities
changing frozen-moment pose/action when only camera viewpoint should change
treating uncertain hardware hypotheses as confirmed metadata

cases.user_request: Match the look of this reference for my own subject and location.
cases.reason: Observable appearance supports visual-DNA transfer but not exact hardware certainty.

cases.user_request: The reference metadata says Sony VENICE 2, 50mm, T2.8. Use that as known metadata and match the visible look.
must_not: downgrade supplied metadata to a visual guess
invent an exact lens model or stock not supplied
cases.reason: Authoritative metadata and direct observation have different provenance and should coexist.

cases.user_request: What lens does this feel like, and recreate that behavior?
must_not: present Cooke Panchro or Canon K35 as confirmed
make the recreation depend on one unverified lens name
cases.reason: Lens-family guesses may be useful hypotheses, but observable optical traits are the reliable transferable layer.

cases.user_request: Use reference A for the person, B for composition and lens feel, and C for lighting and color.
expected_behavior: identity from A must outrank style tendencies in B/C
composition should not copy person from B
lighting/color should not copy incidental scene content from C
must_not: average all three into one undefined style
borrow identity from B or C
let C change composition without instruction
cases.reason: Multi-reference conditioning requires an explicit authority map.

cases.user_request: Match this reference's color, lighting and texture, but my target must stay a true 90-degree top-down shot with deep focus.
expected_transfer: warm soft light if physically compatible
must_not: make target shallow focus just to imitate reference

cases.user_request: Give my desert fashion image the lighting and texture of this motel-room reference.
cases.reason: Visual DNA and incidental subject matter must remain separate.

cases.user_request: Keep the exact same frozen instant, but place the camera over the father's shoulder looking down at the child playing in the sand.
allowed_change: visibility and parallax resulting from camera move
must_not: change lighting to fit the new view
cases.reason: Reference Match must support camera redesign while keeping scene state frozen.

cases.user_request: Turn this convoy reference into a perfect face-down aerial view. Keep the three buggies in the middle and one ATV front and back, all facing the same direction.
target_lock: optical axis perpendicular to ground plane
cases.reason: True top-down geometry and formation preservation are testable independently.

cases.user_request: Use reference A for this exact bottle geometry and label, and reference B for the dramatic lighting only.
expected_behavior: B may alter light/reflection behavior only where it does not alter product design
cases.reason: Product identity/geometry must outrank lighting/style references.

cases.user_request: Use four references: identity, product, location, and lighting. The target provider can accept only two references.
expected_behavior: translate location/lighting DNA into text where possible
must_not: pretend all four references were supplied
change universal shot because provider limit is lower
cases.reason: Reference fallback must preserve authority even when provider conditioning capacity is smaller.
